reader.requirement: In the Inter-Program Communication module the report description entry admits the GLOBAL clause with the X.4.6 semantics (the report-name is a global name, usable from a contained program), and every other RD clause keeps its Report Writer module definition, in any order.

edition-consulted.switches: only the rule a diagnostic cites (CiteRule §1985:XIII.3.5.2 / §2023:13.14.2 in the COBOL2423 at-most-once message); the decision is the same

reader.edition-search: grep of ReportSectionBinder.cs and SymbolTable.Reports.cs for Edition|DialectLevel: the RD clause walk reads Edition only for cited rules (the 2002 PAGE and CODE IS forms are VersionConformancePass constructs, not the GLOBAL clause); InheritReport consults no edition.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no for the RD's GLOBAL clause. (r3_rd_global at --std 2023 is refused COBOL2392 by §2023:14.9.16.3 SR3, a later rule that a contained GENERATE's report file be GLOBAL; COBOL-85's GENERATE (§1985:XIII.4.3) has no such rule, and it is not this rule.)

reader.notes: Re-read on this branch (kb/Work PB2724): the RD rule reportGlobalClause is deleted and reportDescriptionClause's first alternative is the ONE globalClause rule; BindReportDescriptionClauses counts globalClause for the at-most-once screen and sets ReportModel.IsGlobal from it; InheritReport (unchanged) makes a global report visible to contained programs. VersionConformancePass.VisitGlobalClause, which every globalClause host now reaches, gates only a dataDescriptionClause parent in the Linkage Section, so an RD's GLOBAL is never refused by it.

refuter.evidence: Code read independently at the pin, starting from the grammar: `git grep -i globalexternalclause\|reportglobalclause -- src` finds only a historical comment in DiagnosticCatalog.cs, so no reader of the deleted rules survives; fileDescriptionClause, reportDescriptionClause, dataDescriptionClause and constantEntryBody reference the one globalClause, and fileDescriptionClause and dataDescriptionClause the one externalClause. Every consumer of the FD's attributes reads FileModel.IsExternal/IsGlobal (set only in BindFileSection's two arms) or ReportModel.IsGlobal (set only in BindReportDescriptionClauses); OoDefinitionRules.GlobalClauseSites lists the five hosts. The only edition reads on the path are VisitExternalizedNamePhrase (AS, 2002) and VisitGlobalClause, now restricted to a dataDescriptionClause parent in the Linkage Section, which no FD or RD can be. Attacks past the reader's probes at --std 85: x2_rd_code.cob, an RD written 'CODE "AB" IS GLOBAL PAGE 10 LINES' whose report is INITIATEd, GENERATEd and TERMINATEd only in a contained program, wrote 'ABOK' (the CODE prefix kept, GLOBAL accepted between two Report Writer clauses); x3_rd_local.cob, the same INITIATE of an RD without GLOBAL, is refused COBOL1757, so the global attribute comes from the clause and not from the report section.
